planningReadiness.autonomous-plan: Requirements, target files, acceptance criteria, and technical constraints are concrete and settled. The planner can draft an implementation plan without guessing human product preferences or architectural trade-offs.
planningReadiness.discuss-with-user: Requirements are open-ended, under-specified, or involve unresolved product or architectural forks (for example database choice, auth architecture, major dependency changes, or broad scope). Clarify trade-offs with the operator in main chat before delegating to a planner subagent.

difficulty: Exact: fully specified work with named targets, no hidden edge cases, and nothing left to decide.
Ordinary: a settled spec or a bounded change in one area. Routine care is enough.
Hard: ambiguous behavior, several interacting parts, or a review where missed cases are likely without extra care.
Critical: a new system, a major redesign, security or data-loss risk, or a framing that would be expensive to undo.

profiles.description: Code work on a settled spec: directed edits, new tests, performance fixes, and mechanical follow-through. The spec already fixes the interfaces and behavior.

Settled-spec code at full effort: carry out directed edits and tests when interfaces and behavior are already fixed. Unlike adversarial investigation, this is not for finding a cause or redesigning the approach.
Implementation that needs judgment: choosing interfaces, weighing trade-offs, or tracing interacting behavior. Not work with a settled spec.
Adversarial work: migrations, hard debugging, or finding a cause before anything is designed. Not interface design and not a settled-spec edit.
Review or verify existing code: tests, edge cases, and checking that a fix holds. Not new implementation.
Directed tool runs and read-only lookup with exact targets (lint, test, typecheck, build, formatters, named commands); no code writing, no design choices, no git history operations.
Fast exact lookup and bounded command follow-through on a paid subscription. No code writing or design choices.
Fast exact lookup and bounded command follow-through when the target and operation are already named. No code writing or design choices.
Commits, pushes, branches, merges, rebases, tags, and PR updates following the repository's Git flow; writes the commit messages. Not code changes.
Main planner. Writes the plan. Never a review of an existing plan.
Adversarial review of an ordinary written plan: omissions and feasibility. First peer. Do not lead, rewrite, or expand the plan. Not a critical-plan review.
Secondary planner review of a critical written plan: broad scope, a new system, a major redesign, or commitments that are costly to undo. Not an ordinary adversarial pass, and not the main plan.
Seated coordinator. The agent keeps its bound model at high. Decomposes independent work and synthesizes results. Not implementation, not a review, and not a switch to the main planner.
Seated frontier reviewer. The agent keeps its bound model; only effort changes. Ordinary review is high, critical review is xhigh.
Seated primary designer. The agent keeps its bound model; only effort changes.
Seated second designer. The agent keeps its bound model; only effort changes.
